content.intro: This lesson develops topic 122 of the supplied curriculum: **Handling NaN and Infinity**. The main starting point is **- np.isnan()**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Floating-point arithmetic uses finite representations and can accumulate rounding error. Use tolerances, error policies, and non-finite checks that fit the problem.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Handling NaN and Infinity** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **- np.isnan()** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.title: Subtopics from the supplied curriculum

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([1.0, np.nan, np.inf, -np.inf])
print(np.isfinite(values).tolist())

common_mistakes.problem: Comparing approximate results with exact equality
common_mistakes.why: Binary floating-point cannot represent every decimal fraction exactly.
A result can be finite in shape but invalid numerically.
